Legal Standards.name: Reservoir-Specific Storage and Cold Pool Management
Legal Standards.note: Each reservoir operates under site-specific storage and operational specifications, which vary widely by facility and include management of the cold pool to maintain lower-temperature water for downstream uses and ecological protection.

key_elements.definition: Deep reservoir water that maintains colder average temperatures due to sufficient depth

Legal Standards.name: State Water Resources Control Board (SWRCB) Permitting Authority
Legal Standards.note: SWRCB issues permits through separate regulatory processes for water diversion and water storage and monitors compliance with permit conditions governing reservoir releases.

Legal Standards.name: Discretionary Reservoir Release Management
Legal Standards.note: Reservoir releases may be managed discretionarily to satisfy multiple overlapping legal and operational objectives.

objectives: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service requirements

Tier 1.note: Triggers include water year type, biological monitoring, sediment transport, and water temperature; normal operations proceed under standard management.
Stored water is not curtailed; new diversions to storage can be curtailed based on constitutional priorities and rights in time.
Colder/deeper water is used strategically to maintain downstream temperature via mixing and multilevel pumping.

Tier 2.policy_name: Curtailments for junior water rights holders
Tier 2.note: Curtailments occur primarily among junior water rights holders to ensure allocations for senior rights holders; carryover storage generally not in danger.

Triggers modifications to standard operating procedures, permit streamlining for water transfers and groundwater recharge, careful management of existing supplies, and water rights curtailments (even potentially for senior holders).

Tier 3.note: Major changes to operating procedures; state long-term drought/shortage plans implicated. Encouragement of local and regional planning for multi-year periods of little to no deliveries from state and federal projects.

Tier 4.policy_name: Extreme reservoir and water supply management
Tier 4.note: Physical constraints like deadpool dominate operations; severe curtailments and operational modifications occur to preserve basic allocations, potentially affecting all rights holders.
